newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais moves offices in hint of future reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Chubais moves offices in hint of future reshuffle.

text.p: As President Boris Yeltsin kept everyone guessing on Thursday over his cabinet reshuffle, Kremlin-watchers had to fall back on tactics honed in secretive Soviet times to spot who's in and who's out in Moscow.

Interfax news agency reported on a game of musical chairs in the White House government building which recalled the shifting line-up of Soviet leaders assembled above Lenin's tomb on Red Square for big communist parades.

It quoted sources close to Chubais as saying the new reform supremo, named first deputy premier last week, had moved into the office next door to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on the fifth floor of the White House.
"Previously this office was occupied by First Deputy Prime Minister Alexei Bolshakov, who has moved into Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Davydov's office," Interfax said.

"In government circles this was taken as a possible indirect confirmation that Davydov, who is also head of the Ministry of Foreign Trade, might remain only a minister and lose the rank of deputy premier in the reshuffled Russian government."
Yeltsin has made clear that government posts, except those held by Chubais and Chernomyrdin, are up for grabs in the reshuffle, which is aimed at kick-starting market reform.
But while the reshuffle was first announced last week, the shape of a new cabinet remains a closely-guarded secret.
